3:intro: You can configure your workflows to run when specific activity on {% data variables.product.github %} happens, at a scheduled time, or when an event outside of {% data variables.product.github %} occurs.
32:Like {% data variables.product.prodname_actions %} workflows, {% data variables.copilot.agentic_workflows_short %} can be triggered by repository events and schedules. For an example, see [AUTOTITLE](/copilot/how-tos/github-agentic-workflows/creating-github-agentic-workflows).
954:## `schedule`
961:> * {% data reusables.actions.schedule-delay %}
963:> * Scheduled workflows will only run on the default branch.
964:> * In a public repository, scheduled workflows are automatically disabled when no repository activity has occurred in 60 days. For information on re-enabling a disabled workflow, see [AUTOTITLE](/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/disable-and-enable-workflows#enabling-a-workflow).
966:The `schedule` event allows you to trigger a workflow at a scheduled time.
972:     schedule:
976:{% data reusables.repositories.actions-scheduled-workflow-example %}
983:### `actor` for scheduled workflows
985:Certain repository events change the `actor` associated with the workflow. For example, a user who changes the default branch of the repository, which changes the branch on which scheduled workflows run, becomes `actor` for those scheduled workflows.
987:For a deactivated scheduled workflow, if a user with `write` permissions to the repository makes a commit that changes the `cron` schedule on the workflow, the workflow will be reactivated, and that user will become the `actor` associated with any workflow runs.
989:Notifications for scheduled workflows are sent to the user who last modified the cron syntax in the workflow file. For more information, see [AUTOTITLE](/actions/concepts/workflows-and-actions/notifications-for-workflow-runs).
992:> For an enterprise with {% data variables.product.prodname_emus %}, triggering a scheduled workflow requires that the status of the `actor` user account associated with the workflow is currently active (i.e. not suspended or deleted).
993:> * Scheduled workflows will not run if the last `actor` associated with the scheduled workflow has been deprovisioned by the {% data variables.product.prodname_emu %} identity provider (IdP). However, if the last `actor` {% data variables.product.prodname_emu %} has not been deprovisioned by the IdP, and has only been removed as a member from a given organization in the enterprise, scheduled workflows will still run with that user set as the `actor`.
994:> * Similarly, for an enterprise without {% data variables.product.prodname_emus %}, removing a user from an organization will not prevent scheduled workflows which had that user as their `actor` from running.
995:> * Thus, the _user account's_ status, in both {% data variables.product.prodname_emu %} and non-{% data variables.product.prodname_emu %} scenarios, is what's important, _not_ the user's _membership status_ in the organization where the scheduled workflow is located.

content.text:
This is documented, expected behavior — not a bug.

Per `content/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows.md` (`## schedule` section, lines 983–995): the `actor` for a scheduled workflow is whoever last modified the `cron` schedule. Triggering requires that actor's account to be active — deleting/suspending it stops the workflow from running. No warning/email mechanism for this is documented.

Workaround: have another repo collaborator with write access make a commit that touches the cron schedule to reassign the `actor` and reactivate the workflow (line 987).
